en.title: D&D Directors Keep Rolling the Dice on a Sequel Script
en.summary: Despite initial box office disappointment, the directors of **Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves** are actively pitching a sequel script. Hasbro remains committed to finding a new home for the fantasy adventure.
en.body:
It appears the dice haven't stopped rolling for a sequel to **Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves**. Directors **Jonathan Goldstein** and **John Francis Daley** have revealed that a script for a follow-up film is complete and that **Hasbro**, the franchise owner, is actively seeking another studio to bring it to life.

While the 2023 film, starring **Chris Pine**, was met with critical acclaim and fan enthusiasm for its charming take on the beloved tabletop RPG, it struggled to find its footing at the box office. Paramount reportedly passed on a completed sequel script, leaving the future of the cinematic **Dungeons & Dragons** universe in limbo. However, Goldstein and Daley remain optimistic.

> "I think Hasbro is a big believer in it," Goldstein stated in a recent interview, confirming the company's dedication to finding a new home for the project. He added that Hasbro has been making a concerted effort to shop the script around to other major studios, a testament to their commitment despite the first film's financial performance. Daley echoed this sentiment, expressing pride in the unproduced script.

## The Long Road to a Second Quest

The journey for **Dungeons & Dragons** in Hollywood has been a long and winding one, marked by numerous attempts to capture the magic of the game on screen. **Honor Among Thieves** was seen by many as a significant step in the right direction, successfully translating the spirit of adventure, humor, and camaraderie that defines the tabletop experience. The fact that a full script exists and directors are still championing it suggests a strong creative vision for a continuation.

For fans who loved the first film, this news offers a glimmer of hope. The potential for another romp through a fantastical realm with a beloved cast of characters is exciting. The stakes are clear: finding a studio willing to invest in a high-budget fantasy film that, while critically successful, didn't meet initial box office expectations. This situation highlights the complex business of filmmaking, where critical reception and fan passion don't always directly translate into immediate green lights for sequels.

## What's Next for the D&D Cinematic Universe?

While the immediate future of the **Honor Among Thieves** sequel remains uncertain, the news indicates that **Hasbro** is not abandoning its cinematic aspirations for **Dungeons & Dragons**. The company is actively exploring options, and details regarding potential studio partners or a revised production timeline have not yet been announced. In the meantime, fans can keep an eye on **Hasbro**'s other **D&D** TV ventures, including a reported pivot towards the spookier **Ravenloft** setting for a new series.

content_raw: We’ll say this about Hasbro’s decades-spanning efforts to get some serious Hollywood money out of the internationally famous Dungeons & Dragons  brand it’s owned since 1999: They don’t give up easy. Earlier this week , we reported on an apparent pivot in the company’s TV plans for the franchise—dumping a planned series set in the more traditional Forgotten Realms campaign setting for one in the far spookier Ravenloft —that suggested Hasbro’s just going to keep trying stuff until something works. Now, the directors of 2023’s Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves   are out here making the rounds, suggesting plans for a sequel aren’t quite as dire as they initially seemed . The story of Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley’s Honor Among Thieves is pretty well-documented at this point, as critical and fan enthusiasm for the adventurous comedy failed to overcome box office ennui (and whatever curse keeps shoving Chris Pine’s film franchises into a drawer to rot), causing Paramount to turn up its nose at a completed script for a sequel. But, per a recent interview with  The Playlist —timed to their new (and not especially good) Ryan Reynolds/Kenneth Branagh comedy  Mayday —hope for Goldstein and Daley to get the gang back around the table springs eternal in The House That My Little Pony Built.  “I think Hasbro is a big believer in it,” Goldstein said on the podcast, adding that the company has been making a serious effort to shop the script around to another major studio. ( Honor Among Thieves  reportedly cost $150 million to make, so you’re not making this thing on A24 money.) Daley—who spoke of being “proud of the script” for the unproduced film—also reflected a bit on  why  the first movie underperformed at the box office, making a lousy-for-its-budget $200 million. “It was very much a product of not-so-great timing when the first movie came out. It came out four days before the Super Mario movie, which broke records. It came out a month after Wizards Of The Coast changed the official gaming license, prompting many D&D fans to boycott the game , and I don’t think the marketing did enough to tell people who weren’t already fans that this movie might be for them. Yeah, so it was a perfect storm of all of those elements, and we’ll see.”
